chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, who said:

I said to Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام: A woman sees blood for three days or four. He said: "She leaves the salat (prayer)." I said: Then she sees purity for three days or four. He said: "She performs salat (prayer)." I said: Then she sees blood for three days or four days. He said: "She leaves the salat (prayer)." I said: Then she sees purity for three days or four. He said: "She performs salat (prayer)." I said: Then she sees blood for three days or four days. He said: "She leaves the salat (prayer), and she does this for the period between that and one month; then if it stops from her, otherwise she is in the position of the mustahadah (woman in irregular bleeding)."

key_terms.اَلدَّمَ: blood seen by the woman in the context of menstrual or related bleeding
key_terms.اَلصَّلَاةَ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer suspended during menstruation
key_terms.اَلطُّهْرَ: a state of purity in which ritual obligations resume
key_terms.اَلْمُسْتَحَاضَةِ: a woman experiencing irregular bleeding, with distinct legal rulings from menstruation
key_terms.تَدَعُ: she leaves or refrains from performing
key_terms.شَهْرٍ: one month, the time limit mentioned in the ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a woman alternates between menstrual blood and purity over several days?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a woman who alternates between seeing blood and becoming pure over several days. She leaves salat (prayer) during the days of blood and performs salat (prayer) during the days of purity, continuing this pattern up to one month; if the bleeding does not stop, she is treated as a mustahadah.
